booking: Private hire via broker/invite; long waits
note: The best artificial wave on earth, run like a private club: your group alone, a wave count no ocean lineup allows, on-site cabins. Scarcity is the catch — strikeability 4 because you book it like a resort, not a swell.

booking: Book sessions online; private hire available
note: The flagship US pool: scheduled perfect waves, lifeguards, on-site casitas and a lazy river — a genuine resort, which is what qualifies it for the family division when pools are toggled on. Its score also remains the model's calibration diagnostic: it outscores every ocean trip.

booking: Named family weeks only (min age otherwise); 12–18mo
note: Cloudbreak/Restaurants for the chargers, Swimming Pools for improvers, island-capped guest counts, legendary family weeks with kids' programs. As close as it gets to guaranteed world-class waves with a family wrapper.

Purpose-built family surf resort: ~20 breaks for a dozen guests, boat-guided by wave-of-the-tide, pool deck facing the surf, kids' programs. The archetype of 'everyone scores daily' — at expedition distance and price.
Day-club pool with a real range from learner rollers to slabby wedges. No on-site resort — hotels are next door, which is exactly why the family division doesn't headline it.

trip: Central/South atolls resort (Laamu, Six Senses area)
note: Yin Yang and neighbors with a handful out; overwater villas where you watch the sets from the deck. Peak luxury-per-wave, priced accordingly.

booking: Sessions online; on-site lodges; ownership changed 2025 after administration — reconfirm bookings
note: The UK's flagship pool with on-site surf lodges — a genuine stay-and-surf property, so it qualifies for the family division under the resort rule.

Closed 2018, reopened Jan 2024 as Nicaragua's flagship: 12 beachfront villas + 23 bohíos, Tropicsurf resident full-time (10-level coaching, guided boats to 17 breaks), and a private left point with no public road access. The corridor's consistency with Nihi-grade lodging — and a beginner program the boat resorts can't match.
Resort-and-panga model: guides run you to Punta Mango when it's on, mellow inside at Las Flores for improvers, pool terrace above the point. The CR experience of 20 years ago.
Arizona's dual-tech pool — cheap sessions, easy nonstop to Phoenix. Hotels nearby, no resort.

Resort-exclusive lineups (Pasta Point caps surfer numbers by design), warm mechanical walls, dhoni boat shuttles, resort pools and lagoons for the family. The model answer to this brief except distance.
Alpine pool an hour from Geneva — surf in the morning, mountains in the afternoon. No on-site lodging.
Europe's newest large pool, one nonstop from Boston. City hotels, no resort.

booking: Perfect Wave exclusive rights; guest-capped wave; 6–9mo
note: The family-priced Pasta Point analog on an atoll the index didn't cover: exclusive rights to all surf at the resort, Kandooma Right guest-capped, kids-stay-free — a genuine right-hander counterpart to North Malé's lefts at a lower price band.
The Amaru archetype on the SW corridor: 12 design-grade rooms, all-inclusive coaching for every level, and unlimited 4x4 guiding to 10+ breaks on a row whose $ lodges assume you sort yourself out.

booking: Books 6–12mo; wave capped at ~10 surfers/day; from ~$1.5k/night
note: The brief's platonic ideal, priced accordingly: a formal daily cap on a world-class left, resort-exclusive access, full surf program, and an infinity pool directly over the wave. Beginner terrain is coaching-dependent — sits just under the family gate.

The only oceanfront all-inclusive ON the Salina Cruz points (Punta Conejo a 5-min walk), private 4x4 guides, full board — the corridor's camp row upgraded to the Amaru pattern. Risk flag: the Salina Cruz port-expansion breakwater is a documented threat to Punta Conejo itself (wave functioning per 2026 reviews; the guide model covers the whole corridor if it degrades).
Eco surf resorts boating you to soft-top-to-serious reef passes with nobody around; gentler and cheaper than the Namotu circus while still Fiji-consistent.
The southern hemisphere's flagship pool — included for fleet completeness; the flight alone disqualifies it as a pool trip from New England.

A Puro-Surf-grade luxury academy above Dominicalito: 3:1 coach ratio, daily video analysis, chef dining, door-to-door SJO transfer — and supervised coaching directly fixes the rip problem that caps the coastline row's beginner score.

The empty far side of the South Lombok row: 17 clifftop hectares over Inside/Outside Ekas with instructors, infinity pool, and babysitting — the Gerupuk conveyor's crowd tax mostly disappears across the bay.

The Silver Coast's resort-grade family property on the quiet stretch between the Ericeira and Peniche rows: on-sand bungalows, accredited on-site school, everything included (yoga, skate park, bikes, heated pool) — where both sibling rows assume camps and town lodging.

The academy model at its peak: a performance surf school (video analysis, structured coaching, quiver included) wrapped in a boutique hotel whose pool overlooks the El Palmarcito point, with Sunzal-to-Punta-Roca in guided range. The most professionalized coaching product in the hemisphere — a property-level entrant the coastline row couldn't see, added v11.

booking: Gated point community; surf house from ~$99/night all-in
note: The Rancho Santana pattern at $ prices: a quality cobblestone right inside a gated community with limited public access — one of the country's least-crowded good waves — with a beachfront surf house and personal chef.

A different Mentawai zone from the Kandui/HT's row — southern Pagais — with the wave (Macaronis, the world's funnest left) breaking in front of the resort: no daily-boat dependency, pool, kids-under-18-free Decembers, women's clinics. The v4 near-duplicate verdict was wrong; this is the Rancho Santana pattern at Mentawai scale.

The property-level product on the NW corridor the Miramar camps row generalizes: a 13-room all-inclusive surf-and-wellness resort five minutes' walk from The Boom's A-frames, with coaching, guided program, and gentle inside waves for the improvers. Same offshore machine, same emptiness, resort wrapper. Added v13 — the third property the coastline rows hid (after Puro Surf and Rancho Santana), this one surfaced by the owner, not the audits.

The turnkey answer on the SW Nicaragua corridor the index already loves: five private-access beaches, on-site Surf Club (quiver, coaches, daily program), pools and ranch — beginner sand at Los Perros, Panga Drops/Colorado in guided range.

The boys-trip archetype the family lens excluded: a liveaboard chasing the best wave in the archipelago every single day. Wave count no land base can match; cabins, not villas; malaria belt and half-day medevac.

booking: Easier availability than peak; cyclone-season risk
note: The #1 trip's quiet half: cyclone-season swell roulette trims consistency, but the boats, kids' programs, and Swimming Pools all still run, availability opens up, and prices drop a band. Fills the thin Nov–Mar calendar.

Arguably the most consistent learner beach break in the Americas (~330 surfable days/yr), warm water, huge surf-school culture. Crowded because everyone knows it. Overhead outside peaks for advanced; Ollie's Point/Witch's Rock boat day-trips.

The 4x4-guide model at its best: sand-bottom right points (Punta Conejo etc.) picked by wind/tide each morning, lineups effectively gated by access. World-class waves; thin beginner options. Risk flag (2026-08): the port-expansion breakwater is a documented threat to Punta Conejo — wave functioning per 2026 reviews; review this corridor if construction advances.

A near-private cove-and-point 45 min west of the El Tunco crowds, with the pool literally overlooking the break, on-site boards and coaching, and the same 9-consistency S-swell window as the rest of the coast.

booking: Resort easy; Jamie O'Brien Surf Experience on-site
note: Hawaii's only surf school with two commercially private breaks, an exclusive on-site pro program (private, keiki, adaptive), resort-grade everything — the family-viable North Shore trip the DIY winter-base row can't be. Its waves honestly aren't the Seven Mile Miracle; the score says so.
T-Land's long forgiving left wall — an intermediate's dream wave — with sleepy-village emptiness and a few good family lodges.
The world's largest wave pool by area, outside Seoul. Fleet completeness row.

Surfer-founded villa resort directly on Santa Bárbara beach with its own school and beach club — it deletes the Azores row's DIY tax on the shortest real surf flight from Boston. Arguably the best short-haul family property in the index.
Same offshore machine, more variety: Popoyo main peak, Outer Reef for chargers, Beginner's Bay inside. Lodges with pools facing the reef.
Peak S-swell, thinner crowds, afternoon rain. Bigger surf trims the beginner score slightly; mornings still user-friendly.

The longest left on earth: catches any SW swell, and a 2-minute mechanical wall disperses whatever crowd exists. Hotel pools literally overlook the point. Cold-ish water (3/2), grey skies, basic towns.
Boat-to-the-break as daily routine: sheltered bay peaks where every level gets waves every day of dry season. One of the best places on earth to take a mixed-ability crew.
Right-point machine (El Zonte, Sunzal for learners, Punta Roca for experts) 45 min from the airport. Security transformed since 2022; surf-city investment everywhere.
Famara's 5km learner beach under the cliffs plus serious reefs (El Quemao) for experts. Reliable winter machine with European ease.
Guided-only reef pass culture (resorts hold traditional village access), empty by design. Waves are shallow and punchy — thin true-beginner terrain.

booking: Resorts 9–12mo; fixed transfers; some exclude under-12s
note: The best wave zone on the planet, boat-guided daily, resorts increasingly family-capable. But it's expert-centric, malaria-belt remote, and the journey is brutal with kids.
One perfect crescent: kiddie rollers inside, long point walls outside, US ease, breathtaking setting. Winter surf demands respect on big days.

Twelve rooms in the dunes at Punta de Lobos with a guest-exclusive school, spa, and hot tubs — the turnkey answer on a row scored as hardy-DIY. The rubber requirement is unchanged; the thinking is what disappears.
360° peninsula — some bank is always offshore, from Baleal's learner lagoons to Supertubos. Surf-school capital of Europe, with the lineups that implies.
Same offshore machine as Popoyo, far emptier: The Boom's world-class A-frame for the chargers, mellower inside banks for improvers, and camps that run boards, boats, and the daily call.
The quiet Mentawais: mellower reefs (The Peak, Dylan's), a couple of family-run resorts, single-digit lineups. Less wave ceiling, far more forgiving.
Trade-swell island that almost always has something: Freights' gentle left for learners, world-class Soup Bowl for the experts, safe and family-polished everywhere.
The 'European Hawaii': winter N-swells, volcanic reefs on the North Track, big sandy Corralejo bay for learners, warm in January.

booking: Beachfront resort; closed 12 Nov–17 Dec 2026 for renovation
note: The Agadir corridor's only true beachfront family resort: own gentle house break with on-site school, pools, spa, 9km north of the Taghazout crush. Quality trades down — the famous points are a guided drive away.
The Surf Management Plan caps total surfers per break by law — the only formally rationed lineups on earth. Monsoon-season reefs by boat. Getting there is the hardest itinerary on this list.
Right-point conveyor (Anchor Point, Killers) with a mature surf-camp/guide industry and learner beaches between points. Winter crowds are real now.
The budget Telos: tiny island resorts, boat-served zone, near-empty lineups, and Gunturs — a long forgiving right that's one of Sumatra's best learner-to-intermediate waves — on the doorstep.

Lake-effect offshores ~300 days/yr meet relentless SW swell: barreling beach break at your feet, gated community keeps lineups half-private. Panga trips to Lance's Left/Manzanillo. Political situation is calm in surf zones but score docked.
The Nosara-split logic applied to its neighbor: peak S-swell, thinner crowds, cheaper rooms, school-summer timing. Mornings stay learner-friendly; afternoon rain.

booking: Only lodge in the zone; boat program; ~6mo
note: NW Sumbawa's other coastline: the only place to stay in the zone, boat program to near-empty waves, mellow long lefts for improvers — the crowd score the SW-corner row can't offer.
The listed winter row's consistency 7 was the small-season number: summer S-swell is Mita's real season, with the same panga-and-resort turnkey.
Horseshoe bay that grooms S-swell into all-level peaks; genuinely uncrowded midweek. Sleepy but growing scene.

The better family window the winter row obscured: south-shore swell season, Queens and Canoes at their most consistent, and a flat, snorkel-safe North Shore. Beach-boy turnkey at its purest; the crowd is the whole tax.

Saladita: an endless waist-high left made for learning and longboarding. Troncones/The Ranch up the road for punchy waves. Beach-house rentals with pools. Advisory caveat (2026-08 scan): Guerrero is a standing US State Dept Level 4 'Do Not Travel' state — the Zihuatanejo tourist corridor functions normally in practice, but thin medical plus the harshest advisory category cost it the score cut from 7 to 5.5.

booking: Surf lodges bookable; Luanda transit; e-visa
note: The audit's biggest coastline find: a near-Chicama-consistency 300m mellow left, effectively empty, with all-inclusive surf lodges — one directly fronting the point. Beginner and expert ride the same wave. Luanda logistics and thin medical are the caps.
The beginner-optimal El Salvador window: waist-to-head points, offshore mornings, Sunzal at its most learnable, and the crowds gone with the big swells.
Pre-crowd Baleal: small consistent windswell on the learner lagoons, long days, half the September lineup. Lower ceiling than the autumn row — a gentler version of the same trip.
The third member of the capped remote NW-Pacific class (with Kavieng and P-Pass): private-atoll operation, guest-capped, boats and boards provided, empty reef passes. The hardest journey on the list.
Two coasts at right angles: pick your size and wind every day. Warmer and mellower than Peniche; great family towns.
Cold-water Eden: empty reefs and long beginner strands (Strandhill, Tullan) — in a 4/3 with booties. Family charm high if the family owns wetsuits.
Desert surf resorts steps from near-empty right points, with a 40km flat lagoon as the built-in kids' guarantee no other Africa trip has. Wind is the tax — mornings work.

booking: Easy; state-park passes; camps and rentals
note: The canonical US family-longboard trip: Old Man's rollers, Doheny for the kids, Trestles in walking range for the chargers. Everything easy, everyone there — the Waikiki crowd logic applies in full.

The first upscale resort at Lagundri: 16 guests, beachfront at the point, tailored transfers and guiding on a row that assumes losmen walk-ins. Honesty preserved: no property fixes the Point's 60-head circus — crowd stays 4.
World Surfing Reserve: reef points for the experienced, Foz do Lizandro sand for learners, lovely town, red-eye friendly. Everyone in Europe knows it — crowd score suffers.
The offshore machine runs all year; Dec–Mar trades size for friendliness — smaller, cleaner, more learnable, and the calendar's thin months get a $ option.
Palikir Pass is a dream right for good surfers, boat-only, near-empty. Effectively no beginner terrain — a strike mission wearing a family-trip costume.
Black-sand river-mouth waves at Papara for improvers, reef passes and the Teahupoo spectacle for experts, overwater-bungalow family glamour on Moorea. Localism is polite but real.
Manu Bay's endless left plus a proper learner beach (Ngarunui), in a green artsy town. Springsuit water in summer; NZ safety and charm.
Same beach breaks, more swell, meaningfully fewer people than the listed Dec–Apr window.
Ninety-two hectares fronting 5km of near-deserted Itacarezinho beach — resort-grade lodging and a private-feeling learner beach where the town row assumes pousada-DIY.
Private-island boat camp with near-empty waves — rustic, experts-leaning, the budget Pacific-Panama answer to the island-camp class.
Panga-driven longboard points (La Lancha, Anclote) with genuinely gentle waves; five-star family resorts. Sayulita itself is a zoo — stay Mita side.
The best beach-break barrels on earth in September, croissants for the kids, Capbreton's protected corner for learners. Shifty banks punish beginners on bigger days.
Bali's swell without Bali's chaos: boat-accessed reefs (Playgrounds for improvers, Lacerations for experts), family resorts with pools facing the lineup.

The Las Flores resort-and-panga model on the Caribbean: max ~10 surfers, daily boat calls to 15 waves within 20 minutes (Silverbacks in range) on a row that assumes DIY boat-hiring. Swell-dependence is unchanged — the window still decides the trip.
The shortest real flight to empty Atlantic surf from Boston. Black-sand beach breaks and reefs, whales and hot springs for flat days. Weather-roulette — swell and wind change fast.
The summer-Hawaii family trip, distinct from winter Hanalei: reliable south swell rollers, resort infrastructure, learner-perfect inside.
Gentle winter rollers at Launiupoko and Puamana for the family, Honolua Bay's world-class right up the road when the north swell lands.

booking: Losmen and small camps; near walk-in
note: Sumatra's mainland conveyor: a dozen quality lefts and rights around a sleepy town at backpacker prices. Long overland haul; thin medical.
Warm, cheap, endlessly mellow — a dozen learner-to-intermediate reefs and beaches in 20km, great food and family villas. Blew up post-2020; lineups show it.

Family-run island surf resort with daily boats to uncrowded fun reefs — the only family-gate-passing trip in the entire Nov–Apr remote-Pacific window, which the calendar otherwise cedes to experts-first Kavieng and Pohnpei.

booking: Easy; book flights early for school weeks
note: Easiest CR logistics, very learner-friendly, boat trips to Witch's Rock. Heavily touristed — the crowd score pays for the convenience.
Gentle Basque beach breaks, world-best food, culture days built in. A family holiday with very good surf rather than a surf trip.
The Bay: a 600m+ gentle right where a first-timer rides for 30 seconds — maybe the best learner wave anywhere. Village amenities are simple; longboarders flock to it.
Two-coast peninsula — swell always hitting one side — with Ngor Right of Endless Summer fame, established island camps doing boards and guiding, and Yoff sand for learners.
Sea lions in the lineup, N-swell reef points with almost nobody out, plus the wildlife trip of a lifetime for kids. Logistics and cost are the gate.
The other, better-served half of Sumbawa the list had skipped: Scar Reef and Supersuck for the chargers, Jelenga inside for the rusty.
Uncrowded black-sand beach break village — simple, cheap, consistent. Punchy shorebreak days need supervision for kids.

Genuinely uncrowded, consistent Atlantic beach breaks with European safety. Note correction (2026-08 sweep): a real camp ecosystem exists (Artsurfcamp at Razo runs full coached weeks), so the old 'self-assemble only' verdict was stale — turnkey raised 5 → 6; still no resort-grade property.
Dawn-patrol reef peaks that suit surf schools remarkably well; kite/windsurf afternoons for the rest of the family. Short cheap flights.
The consistent central-Pacific window the CR coverage was missing. Punchy beach break with real rips — beginner score capped accordingly.
Friendly peaks and a proper learner scene; shuttle-truck culture from SJDS. Busier than the private-community options.
Consistent beach breaks for all levels, great food/lodging scene, but discovered — lineups busy and the drive in is long.
Zicatela is the Mexican Pipeline — spectate, don't bring the kids out. La Punta and Carrizalillo cove are the family end. Town is buzzing and busy.
Powerful world-class right point, empty by CR standards. Estero beach break for learners, but the town is basic and the drive long.
Resort-corridor convenience with a real summer wave (The Rock, Old Man's for learners). Easy, warm, but lineups concentrate.
Typhoon-season swell, boat trips to uncrowded reefs beyond Cloud 9, palm-island charm, very affordable. Swell windows less locked-in than Indo; typhoon risk is real.
The mainland's gentlest learner beach plus reef options up the coast. US-easy everything; the crowd is the price.
The Caribbean side the 100%-Pacific CR coverage skipped: Salsa Brava for the chargers, Cocles sand for learners, a 3-month window and Limón-province edge.
Fixes the Guadeloupe row's own named cap: an institutional week with 10 coached sessions, gear, and spot rotation included, at sports-association prices. Lodging is hostel-grade — that's the trade.
Winter NW swell, learner-friendly Cerritos, artsy Todos Santos base. Water is cool (springsuit) and the surf is fun rather than world-class.
Relentless left points, but 4/3-and-booties cold even in summer. A surf trip for a hardy family, not a tropical one.
Long sand-bottom right points (Main Point, Whiskey, Peanut Farm) with tuk-tuk guide culture. The far side of a long journey.
The easiest real surf trip from New England: no passport, US healthcare, winter N-swells lighting up a dozen breaks from mellow to Tres Palmas. Swell-dependent weeks and busy peaks are the tax.
World-class empty points on a safe, easy-to-reach island — with boulder entries and no sand anywhere. An experts-first row, same treatment as J-Bay.
The Mexican Pipeline as a base, not a spectacle: the existing row is La Punta-configured for families; this is the row for a crew that came to ride Zicatela itself.
Dry-season perfection every single day — shared with the entire surfing world. The crowd score is the story; cliff-top pools do overlook the breaks.

Rescored as Waikiki-only after the audit caught the base-pairing error: the winter row had been charging North Shore quality a mixed family can't ride. Winter south shore is smaller but rideable most days; the North Shore is a spectacular spectator day, not a program. See the summer row for this trip's better family window.
The East Coast's best sandbars, drivable, with hurricane-season swell — and the two things the brief punishes: a week can skunk, and chasing the right bank IS the OBX game.

Soup Bowl's actual prime — hurricane swells with 3-5 days of forecast lead, a nonstop flight, and half-price hotels. Rejected as a book-ahead row in v4 (consistency lottery); re-admitted as the strike division's East Coast classic.
Desert left points, warmer than Chicama, Máncora has the family beach scene. Oil-town grit around Lobitos.
One of the world's great rights, machine-consistent — and a 60-head circus on every swell since the seabed uplift. The famous wave does not fix waves-per-person.

The boys-mode Oahu row the family lens excluded: based at the Seven Mile Miracle, dawn-patrolling Haleiwa and Chun's with the world's best out at Pipe. Realized wave count is honest — the deepest pecking order on earth caps it.
Surfers' Corner is a legendary learn-to-surf beach, and Cape Town is a spectacular family city. Busy lineups, cool water, shark protocol managed by spotters.
Caribbean N-swell window — reef and beach options by boat, island-hopping fun. Swell-dependent: flat spells happen.
Warm N-swell season, mellow Ayampe beach break with a quiet yoga-town vibe (skip Montañita's party for the family). Cheap and uncrowded.
Supertubes is the best right point on the planet, and winter delivers it weekly. Learner beaches exist, water's cold, and it's a very long way with kids for a wave only the experts ride.
Seven-mile jungle left with all-inclusive camps at the wave. Canonical advanced trip; zero learner terrain — added for universe completeness after being excluded on family grounds.
Brazil's Hawaii: crystal N-swell peaks, capped visitor numbers keep it empty, spectacular for kids (dolphins, snorkeling). Expensive and far.
Perfect sandy points wrapping through a national park — when cyclone swell arrives, and with 200 longboarders. A glorious family beach town whose surf score is hostage to swell roulette and crowds.
Hurricane-groomed points 90 minutes' flight from Boston, nearly empty, in 4/3 water. The cold-water short-haul row the bias audit said was missing.

booking: Schools and camps plentiful; school-holiday crowds
note: The densest wetsuits-included family-surf-school industry on earth, in a lovely holiday coast — with UK summer crowds and UK summer swell.

booking: PRIMARY OPERATOR CEASED — Ha'atafu Beach Resort destroyed by the Jan 2022 tsunami, listed ceased as of 2025; verify any operator before planning
note: Score correction (2026-08 property sweep): the resort this row's turnkey/lodging were premised on was destroyed by the Hunga Tonga tsunami and is confirmed ceased. The reef and the whales remain; the turnkey trip as modeled does not, until a new operator is verified.
A-frame perfection with a pool-bar audience at Lakey's losmen row. More surf-trip than family-trip; long haul.
Warm jungle-backed coves with reliable small-to-mid surf — a lovely learn-and-longboard family spot rather than a quality strike.
Steady trade windswell reefs and a proper French-island family holiday. Quality ceiling and turnkey are the caps — the near-nonstop Caribbean depth row.
42 beaches on one island — always a working bank somewhere. Autumn/winter is consistent and less crowded; water cools to springsuit.
NE-monsoon windswell points on a friendly, cheap, safe coast. A pleasant B-trip shown for completeness — the audit's verdict stands.

The shortest warm-water learner trip from New England — small, mushy, crowded, and shark-nippy, but 3 hours door to airport and surf schools everywhere. Shown, as the audit demanded, rather than silently absent.
Japan's most consistent coast in typhoon season: fun beach breaks, immaculate logistics, onsen recovery — and a swell lottery the consistency weight rightly punishes.

booking: Scorpion Bay Hotel operating (online booking, restaurant, rentals); trip remains a swell-chase expedition
note: On a real S-swell: multiple points connecting into minute-long rights, nearly empty. But it needs the swell and getting there is an expedition. Score is honest about the gamble.
One of the world's longest lefts when a proper S-swell lands — but it needs that swell. Boom-or-bust; remote; limited family lodging.

booking: Strike only: fly when the chart confirms; some years it never breaks
note: The longest sand-bottom barrel on earth, breaking a handful of days a year off one specific storm track. Pure strike asset: worthless to book ahead (consistency 3), priceless when the chart lights up — visible ~5 days out, which is exactly enough.
